Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-13 16:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM); Aisha Khan (KiteWave CTO), Daniel Romero (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Head of AI)

Summary (auto):
Brief discovery covering time-to-first-token plan, hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs, security controls (SOC2/KMS/SSO), and quickstart credits. Agreed to send security pack and schedule technical deep dive for private deployment.

Topics: Quickstart path, free credits, time-to-first-token (TTFT), Dedicated vs VPC, KMS & data residency, latency vs cost, rollout plan

Transcript: (imperfect; occasional mis-hears and filler)
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick run through the agenda, we're gonna cover the free credits quickstart, where teams usually get to first call in under an hour, and then go into hosting choices — hosted, dedicated reserved pools, and the private VPC/on-prem path. Ravi's gonna field the deep infra questions.
[00:18] Aisha: Thanks, Jordan. We're pretty interested in how fast we can prototype. For context, KiteWave does personalized content generation for newsletters and realtime snippets in-app. We care about P95 latency under 200ms for the short completion paths, and obviously security - all of our production traffic must be inside our VPC or meet strict data residency.
[00:40] Daniel: Yeah, we also measure cost per 1k tokens and want predictable spend. We're evaluating a couple of vendors and also an internal runtime team.
[00:50] Ravi: Cool. Quick qualification: is this for an internal prototype only, or do you expect to flip into production in Q4?
[00:58] Priya: Prototype now, but likely small production by mid Q1. We have a compliance review in Nov so things need to be buttoned up.
[01:12] Jordan: Got it. Our usual path: we give free credits for the PLG quickstart — you'll get a sandbox API key to call our hosted inference immediately. Most teams hit first token in under 15 minutes using our SDK and curl examples. Then you can either continue on hosted, or step into Dedicated (reserved capacity) for predictable throughput, or Private which is a VPC connector or on-prem package if you need full network isolation.
[01:35] Aisha: For Private, do you ship anything inside our network or do we bring the package to our cluster? How does KMS work?
[01:44] Ravi: For the VPC/private option we offer a customer-managed control plane that talks to a lightweight agent in your VPC. You can integrate with your KMS/HSM for key wrapping. Our Private distribution can be air-gapped in the on-prem package; in that scenario audit logs stay local. The usual confusion is between "dedicated" and "private" — dedicated is still Redwood-managed infra but reserved to you, private is where you get the control plane or agent in your environment.
[02:10] Daniel: Ok, that helps. On the latency target, you said many customers get <200ms, is that cold-start or steady-state?
[02:20] Ravi: That's steady-state with batching tuned for short sequences. Cold-starts depend on model and whether KV cache is warm. We can give the latency profile for a specific model and sequence length; I'll run a quick estimate for your 100-token average and expected qps.
[02:36] Aisha: Also, can you speak to model variants and fallback — if capacity is constrained do you fallback to a smaller quantized variant? We can't have degraded responses silently change behavior in prod.
[02:49] Jordan: Yes, smart routing/fallbacks are configurable — we don't do silent model swaps without notifying the client. You can set policy: strict exact model, or allow fallback with annotated responses so you can track when fallback happened.
[03:05] Priya: About security: we need SOC2 type II evidence, SAML/SSO integration, RBAC, and request-level audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Can all of that be produced with Redwood Private?
[03:18] Maya: Yep, and also with Dedicated for most audit and RBAC needs. SOC2 reports live in our security bundle, and we can provide SSO via SAML/Okta; audit logs can be shipped to customer endpoints or kept in Redwood's logs with export. For Private/on-prem you control log retention.
[03:36] Daniel: Any gotchas with egress? If we run VPC connector, is traffic proxied through Redwood's control plane?
[03:43] Ravi: The data plane for inference stays in the region you choose; the control plane coordinates. For strict egress restrictions we recommend the on-prem package. The VPC connector will create outbound connections to Redwood endpoints for orchestration but we can set up minimal pinned IP ranges and peering.
[03:58] Aisha: Ok, we need to show this to procurement — what about contracts for Dedicated? Is there a commit term?
[04:06] Jordan: Dedicated is typically monthly or annual reserved capacity. We can do short pilots on hosted and then move to a committed dedicated pool once you have expected throughput. Pricing spreadsheet I'll send after the call.
[04:16] Daniel: For prototyping we prefer to avoid long-term commitments until we validate latency and quality. So free credits and a hosted pilot is ideal.
[04:24] Jordan: Perfect. We'll get you credits. The quickstart playbook covers SDK setup, sample prompts, how to run load locally to emulate 1k qps, and quick evals.
[04:33] Priya: Speaking of prompts — our use-case will concat user context plus templates and sometimes up to ~800 tokens. Does Redwood support streaming and function/tool calls? We plan to use tool calls to fetch user profiles.
[04:46] Ravi: Yes, streaming is supported for both chat and generation, and we support structured tool calling. For the 800-token flows you might want to evaluate quantized variants for cost, but that can affect output quality; Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per workload.
[05:03] Aisha: You mentioned Optimize; do you do automated suggestions based on traffic?
[05:08] Jordan: Redwood Optimize will recommend batching/cache settings and model/quantization choices for the workload pattern you feed it. We can run an initial analysis if you share sample traffic patterns.
[05:18] Daniel: One of our devs' concern is SDK integration — we use Go and node microservices. Any quickstart libs?
[05:25] Jordan: We have official SDKs for Python, Node, and Go; plus CLI and curl examples. Most customers wire up the first calls in <30 minutes. The free credits show up in the Console and you can create API keys per environment.
[05:36] Priya: On monitoring, do you expose per-route token breakdowns and tracing? We need to correlate model cost to product flows.
[05:43] Maya: Yes, the Console has token-level cost, latency, per-model breakdown, and tracing hooks. You can map keys to teams and route models per team as well.
[05:53] Aisha: What's the usual TTFT for us? If we want to get to our first real response in our staging environment, what's realistic?
[05:59] Ravi: If you follow the quickstart playbook, create the API key, install the SDK, and run a sample prompt, most teams get to first token in under 15 minutes. Realistic time to full pipeline (tooling + CI + staging) is a day or two, depending on infra.
[06:12] Daniel: You said most customers test with smaller concurrency; for our 1k qps target do you recommend starting on hosted and then move to dedicated?
[06:20] Ravi: Yes, start hosted to validate prompt quality and integrations, then if you need sustained throughput and guaranteed latency, move to Dedicated reserved capacity. For strict data controls and regulatory constraints, go private.
[06:31] Priya: Do you have customers running high-volume workloads on Dedicated? Any reference architecture or benchmarks?
[06:37] Jordan: We do — media companies and adtech at scale. I'll share a benchmark deck and a spreadsheet that maps tokens per second to GPU pools and cost estimates.
[06:46] Aisha: Great. A couple of specific questions from procurement: encryption at rest, BYOK via KMS, and how long logs are retained by default?
[06:56] Maya: By default logs are retained 90 days in hosted; you can request longer retention as an add-on. Encryption at rest is on by default and we support BYOK via KMS integrations. For private deployments you manage keys.
[07:10] Daniel: For the VPC agent, what about upgrades and patching? We want minimal operational burden.
[07:16] Ravi: The agent is lightweight and supports rolling upgrades. For the on-prem air-gapped package we provide the upgrade artifacts and a runbook. For VPC connectors we manage most upgrades with a maintenance window that we coordinate.
[07:30] Aisha: One more question — how do you handle PII? If we send user content for generation, can we opt out of retention?
[07:38] Maya: Yes, you can disable retention for certain keys, and with Private you keep all logs local. Hosted can be configured with zero-retention policies per customer if needed. We'll include details in the security bundle.
[07:50] Jordan: Quick aside — competitors: you mentioned OpenAI and Anthropic; the difference we're pitching is production controls, batching/cost tooling, and a consistent API across hosted/dedicated/private. Not trying to disparage, just positioning.
[08:05] Priya: Understood. For our security review in Nov, we'll need SOC2 docs, pen test reports, and the KMS integration guide.
[08:13] Jordan: We'll put that together and send the security whitepaper + SOC2 contact.
[08:18] Aisha: Thanks. If we do a pilot, what's the minimum duration and what's in scope?
[08:24] Jordan: Pilot on hosted is flexible — 2 weeks to a month is common. We include credits, onboarding support from an SE, and a small performance benchmark run. If you want Dedicated pilot we typically set up a short reserved pool for the pilot period.
[08:36] Daniel: On the benchmarking — will you run end-to-end tests from our VPC if we go private?
[08:42] Ravi: Yes, for private deployments we can run bench tests inside your environment; we'll need ephemeral credentials and a test harness.
[08:48] Priya: Could we get a sample SSO integration doc? We use Okta.
[08:52] Maya: We'll include SAML/Okta setup steps in the security pack.
[08:56] Jordan: Quick recap and next steps — we'll: 1) send security bundle and SOC2; 2) activate free credits in KiteWave account and share quickstart playbook; 3) Ravi will follow up with latency/cost estimates tied to your 1k qps / 100 token avg; 4) schedule a technical deep-dive for 2026-10-20 to scope Private/VPC. Anything missing?
[09:18] Aisha: That sounds right. One request — include a short checklist of what we need to prepare for the Nov compliance review.
[09:24] Jordan: Will do.
[09:26] Daniel: Thanks everyone.
[09:28] Jordan: Thanks, we'll send notes.
